players.product: On-site power generation for AI data centers and large loads (Liberty Power Innovations: multi-OEM engine generation stacks with BESS, energy management and ERCOT/PJM market participation)

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Ron Gusek: Liberty has made a public announcement around Energy Service Agreements that will be coming — 'We said we will announce more than 500 megawatts of Energy Service Agreements before the end of the year.' He said Liberty is well on its path to deploying 3 gigawatts of power by 2029, with line of sight to all of that inbound.
quarterly_data.figure: more than 500 megawatts of Energy Service Agreements to be announced before the end of the year; 3 gigawatts by 2029

quarterly_data.signal: Partner Vantage: CEO Ron Gusek said Liberty already has 'a couple of big public partnerships out there, Vantage, likely for a site up in Wyoming for 400 megawatts and some others coming over and above that.'

CEO Ron Gusek: partnerships with Oklo and Fervo, amongst others, give Liberty a path to next-generation technologies — starting customers with natural gas fired generation for speed to market, then introducing more sophisticated, lower-emission technologies to the energy stack as the grid arrives, to help hyperscalers meet their stated objectives. He said Liberty intends to be the primary power provider: the grid brings benefits but 'won't displace what we do', and hyperscalers 'have realized over the last 12 months that the grid is not going to aid them' in getting to compute quickly.

CEO Ron Gusek on the origin of the power business: Liberty vertically integrated into power generation to control energy supply for its electric frac fleets, and for the last five, six years has run five mobile power generation plants that generate 25 to 30 megawatts of electricity on location in remote environments, with fuel supply Liberty delivers; that expertise let it step into power generation for data centers. He said Liberty is now a licensed power producer in both PJM and ERCOT, with load management and grid interaction capabilities.
quarterly_data.figure: five mobile power generation plants of 25 to 30 megawatts each

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Ron Gusek on AI in Liberty's operations: Liberty moves more than 20 million tons of sand a year (more than 1 million truckloads), and deploying AI in logistics cut the number of trucks required by 35%; it streams about 2 billion data points into 'The Hive', an LLM overseeing all rotating equipment, and component longevity (engines, transmissions, power ends) has climbed by as much as 100% since the AI model began overseeing maintenance; an agentic AI model to execute frac jobs is on test on probably a third of its fleets. He said Liberty has not laid off a single person because of AI.
quarterly_data.figure: more than 20 million tons of sand a year; trucks reduced by 35%; about 2 billion data points; component longevity up as much as 100%; agentic AI on test on a third of fleets

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Ron Gusek on the completions business: Liberty's cash return on capital invested has been 23% over the last 15 years, with a low of -2% and a high of 44 or 45%; when Liberty started there were 450 frac crews and 1,800 rigs in North America versus 200 frac crews and a third of the rigs today at record oil and natural gas production, so efficiency gains mean Liberty will 'have to grow to stay flat in that business' and needed new businesses; he believes the frac business has a long runway.
quarterly_data.figure: 23% cash return on capital invested over 15 years (low -2%, high 44 or 45%); 450 frac crews then vs 200 today; 1,800 rigs then

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Ron Gusek macro view: 25% of the world's LNG used to pass through the Strait of Hormuz, and the six-month disruption has removed of order maybe 2.5 billion barrels of oil from the global market; 'there is no energy transition going on', it is an energy addition story — oil, gas and coal are still about 85% of global energy supply, and since 2010 demand grew from about 500 exajoules to about 625 exajoules with those fuels meeting about 75% of the increment. With the 'lucky one billion' consuming about 13 barrels of oil per person per year versus about 3 for the other 7 billion, he sees a 'massive' long-term outlook for oil and natural gas, and says AI's energy demand is 'not insignificant', with natural gas fueled generation being stood up to drive compute.
quarterly_data.figure: 25% of world LNG via Hormuz; maybe 2.5 billion barrels removed over 6 months; about 85% fossil share; 500 to 625 exajoules; 13 vs 3 barrels per person per year
